title: Microbudgeting for feature flags: headcount triggers & price tests (Apr 2026)
content:
Purpose and context:
Quick working sheet to test microbudgeting approach for new feature-flag driven product initiatives (small experiments that might scale). Goal: map small incremental headcount + infra delta per feature cohort, and understand how price movement (token price compression or premium) interacts with runway and hiring triggers. This is intentionally lightweight (sheet-first), to iterate with product on realistic trigger points.

High-level assumptions (please review):
- Time window: 12 months (Apr 2026 -> Mar 2027).
- Base company burn (fixed opex excluding these features): $3.1M/month.
- Feature cohort scoping: 5 independent feature flags being piloted; each cohort initially supported by a small cross-functional pod (0.6 FTE eng, 0.2 FTE ML, 0.15 FTE product, 0.05 FTE SWE-ops).
- Fully-loaded FTE costs (incl benefits, burden, recruiting) estimate: Eng = $220k/yr, ML = $240k/yr, Product = $170k/yr, SWE-ops = $200k/yr.
- Hiring lag: 8 weeks from approval-to-first-day.
- Burst infra (GPU) incremental per active cohort: baseline 0.75 GPU-months at $5,000/GPU-month (weighted across spot/commit mix).
- Token economics: current blended token yield = $0.00011/token (hosted price to customers). Sensitivity tests: -20%, -10%, 0%, +10% (customer price movement / realized revenue per token).
- Conversion to revenue sensitivity: assume feature adoption increases token usage per customer by cohort mean 12% (varies by cohort).

Microbudget model (per cohort, monthly):
- Labor monthly cost per cohort pod = (0.6*Eng + 0.2*ML + 0.15*Product + 0.05*SWEops)/12
  = (0.6*220k + 0.2*240k + 0.15*170k + 0.05*200k)/12
  = ($132k + $48k + $25.5k + $10k)/12 = $215.5k/12 = $17,958/month (rounded $18k)
- Infra monthly per cohort = 0.75 * $5,000 = $3,750
- Tooling / infra misc = $1,200/month (logging, evals, small infra ops)
- Total incremental cost per cohort (month 1 after hire) = $23k/month (rounded)

Trigger design (operational hooks):
- Trigger A (adoption-based): if cohort usage lift >8% and retention delta >2ppt after 6 weeks -> greenlight hire (one pod).
- Trigger B (cost-benefit): if projected incremental revenue from token uplift over 6 months > 2x cumulative incremental cost -> scale to 2 pods.
- Trigger C (stop or freeze): if token-price compression >15% simultaneously with <5% adoption lift -> freeze hires and cap infra.

Scenarios (rolling 12-month projection):
1) Baseline (no price change, average adoption): assume 3 of 5 cohorts hit Trigger A in months 2–4, one hits B by month 6, none hit C.
   - New pods hired: 4 (phased). Peak incremental monthly cost at month 7 = 4 * $23k = $92k.
   - Annual incremental spend (for these cohorts) = sum(monthly, factoring ramp/hire lag) ≈ $520k.
   - Runway impact: with current burn, runway shortens by ~1.8 weeks relative to plan.

2) Price compression -20% (customer price pressure; realized revenue per token down 20%):
   - Revenue from cohorts drops proportionally; many cohorts no longer meet Trigger B. Two cohorts freeze mid-Q2 (Trigger C). Hires paused.
   - Hired pods: 2. Peak incremental monthly = 2*$23k = $46k.
   - Expected reduction in gross margin leads to tighter runway: runway shortens by ~5 weeks vs plan.
   - Operational note: if compression persists >3 months we should consider temporary hiring freeze across all microbudget cohorts.

3) Price uplift +10% (upside scenario):
   - More cohorts meet Trigger B by month 4; we scale to 6 pods (some cohorts get second pod). Peak incremental monthly = 6*$23k = $138k.
   - Additional revenue likely to cover incremental cost in months 3–9. Net result: runway improves by ~2 weeks (due to faster payback).

Sensitivity table (summary) - simple view for CFO quick scan:
- Variable: token revenue per token change -> delta run rate impact (12-month)
   - -20%: incremental annual spend (cohorts) -20% (but less hires) => runway delta: -5 weeks
   - -10%: runway delta: -3 weeks
   - 0%: runway delta: -1.8 weeks (baseline)
   - +10%: runway delta: +2 weeks

Payback back-of-envelope (per pod):
- Incremental revenue required to pay for one pod per month = $23k.
- If average incremental token uplift yields $0.00011/token, cadence to payback = 23,000 / 0.00011 ≈ 209 million extra tokens/month (this is illustrative — convert to customer usage counts depending on product).
- More useful KPI: revenue per active customer per month (ARPA). If cohort adds $3 ARPA on 8k customers -> $24k/mo ~ covers pod.

Actionable recommendations (short list):
- Move to approval gate: authorize up to 3 pods as a pilot (cap) for Apr-July with weekly dashboarding.
- Implement token-price watch: automated alert if blended realized token revenue drops >8% month-over-month for 2 consecutive weeks -> temporary pause on pod approvals. Link to slack alert channel: finance-prod-price-watch.
- Add micro-control in hiring req: any pod hire requires a 2-line justification mapping to trigger A/B. Recruiters to include "microbudget cohort" tag in req to track.
- Run a 6-week internal experiment: price-test a feature cohort with a 10% promo (A/B) to validate elasticity and adoption uplift — finance should model the marginal revenue into a quick dashboard.

Open questions / risks (to resolve with Product & SRE):
- Do we have telemetry to measure "adoption lift" within 4 weeks per cohort reliably? (ACTION: @Ava Chen to confirm event instrumentation, JIRA: FIN-OBS-77)
- If token revenue moves, how fast can price pass-through be executed to customers (contracting constraints)?
- GPU spot availability risk: if spot spike >40% we should expand infra budget or throttle cohorts. Who owns the throttle? (SRE ops owner needed)

Appendix: quick monthly sketch (sample months, numbers are rounded)
Month 0 (Apr): pilot 1 cohort, infra and 0.6 FTE fraction through contractors -> incremental $14k
Month 2: cohort 1 hires full pod -> +$23k; cohort 2 starts contractor -> +$12k (lagging)
Month 4: cohorts 1,2,3 active pods -> incremental monthly run-rate ~$69k
Month 7: peak as some cohorts scale second pod -> incremental monthly run-rate ~$138k (upside)

Next steps / owners:
- Priya Nair: finalize microbudget template and push to shared drive (this sheet) by Apr 15.
- Marcus Patel: wire up quick dashboard (Looker/QuickSight) to show adoption lift & token ARPA per cohort by Apr 22.
- Ava Chen: confirm instrumentation and list of events by Apr 12 (blocking).
- Jonah Ruiz: create hiring-requisition tagging pattern with Talent Ops by Apr 20.

- Slack: #product-experiments, #finance-planning

Rough TODOs (one-line):

-- end of working sheet (notes, not final).
Notes: keep this as a living doc — expect numbers to change after instrumentation is confirmed. Treat hiring triggers as soft until we validate payback on actual token uplift.
